questions.knowledge_point: Using a Percentage Points Table To Find the Z-Score for a Given Probability
questions.problem:
The table below gives the values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p,$ where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. Find the value of $z$ such that $P(Z\le z)=0.999.$

| $\,p\,$ | $0.900$ | $0.950$ | $0.975$ | $0.990$ | $0.995$ | $0.999$ | $0.9995$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.9600\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ | $\,2.5758\,$ | $\,3.0902\,$ | $\,3.2905\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express the given information in terms of $Φ:$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\le z) & =0.999 \\ Φ(z) & =0.999\end{aligned}
$$

So, we are looking for the value of $z$ such that

$$
z={Φ}^{-1}(0.999).
$$

We look for the column in the table that corresponds to $p=0.999,$ and we find that

$$
p=0.999\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(p)=3.0902.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
z={Φ}^{-1}(0.999)=3.0902.
$$

questions.problem:
The table below gives the values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p,$ where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. Find the value of $z$ such that $P(Z>z)=0.30.$

| $\,p\,$ | $0.55$ | $0.60$ | $0.65$ | $0.70$ | $0.75$ | $0.80$ | $0.85$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.1257\,$ | $\,0.2533\,$ | $\,0.3853\,$ | $\,0.5244\,$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express the given information in terms of $Φ,$ using the complement:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z>z) & =0.30 \\ 1-P(Z\le z) & =0.30 \\ 1-Φ(z) & =0.30 \\ Φ(z) & =1-0.30 \\ Φ(z) & =0.70\end{aligned}
$$

So, we are looking for the value of $z$ such that

$$
z={Φ}^{-1}(0.70).
$$

We look for the column in the table that corresponds to $p=0.70,$ and we find that

$$
p=0.70\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(p)=0.5244.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
z={Φ}^{-1}(0.70)=0.5244.
$$

questions.problem:
The table below gives the values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p,$ where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. Find the value of $z$ such that $P(Z\le z)=0.025.$

| $\,p\,$ | $0.965$ | $0.970$ | $0.975$ | $0.980$ | $0.985$ | $0.990$ | $0.995$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,1.8119\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,1.9600\,$ | $\,2.0537\,$ | $\,2.1701\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ | $\,2.5758\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
From the table, notice that

$$
P(Z\le 1.9600)=0.975.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
P(Z\ge 1.9600)=1-0.975=0.025.
$$

By the symmetry of the standard normal distribution, we have

$$
Φ(-1.9600)=0.025.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070279/assets/8a3513b66e17745585f5f49ea3cb1b1c7241874159e3cfaca0e5f644d0b7a3c2.png)

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-1.9600) & =0.025 \\ P(Z\le -1.9600) & =0.025.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required value of $z$ is $-1.9600.$
